Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 78, verses 1–3:

**Naming of the surah**

• It is called al-Naba' (The Tidings), because it opens with a question about the question the polytheists asked concerning the great tidings (al-naba' al-'azim), which is the Day of Resurrection.

**Some of the surah's objectives**

• Speaking about the Resurrection (al-qiyamah), the raising of the dead (al-ba'th), and the recompense (al-jaza'), mentioning the stance of those who deny the raising and warning them, establishing proofs and evidences of God's power to resurrect creation after their death, describing the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, mentioning the punishment prepared for the disbelievers and the bliss prepared for the believing God-fearing (al-muttaqun), in keeping with the Qur'an's method of combining encouragement (tarhib... al-targhib) and warning (al-tarhib).

[Tafsir]

About what do some of the disbelievers of Quraysh ask one another? They question one another about the tremendous, great tidings, which is the Mighty Qur'an that informs of the resurrection (al-ba'th), about which the disbelievers of Quraysh doubted and denied.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 78, verse 21–26:

Indeed, Hell was lying in wait, (21) a place of return for the disbelievers, (22) remaining in it for ages upon ages, one after another without end. (23) They will not taste therein anything that cools the heat of the Blaze for them, (24) nor any drink that quenches them, (25) except boiling water and the pus of the people of the Fire. (26) They will be recompensed with this, a just recompense, corresponding to their deeds which they used to do in the world.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 78, verses 27–30:

They did not fear the Reckoning, so they did not act in preparation for it, and they denied what the Messengers brought them, a complete denial. And We have recorded everything in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). So taste, O disbelievers, the recompense of your deeds; We will increase you in nothing but punishment upon your punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 78, verses 31–35:

Indeed, for those who fear their Lord and do righteous deeds, there is a triumph: their entry into Paradise. Indeed, for them are great gardens and grapevines, and for them are wives of equal age, with full, rounded breasts, all of the same age, and for them is a cup filled with wine. In this Paradise they will not hear any vain speech, nor will they lie to one another.

Indeed, for them are great gardens and grapevines, and for them are wives of equal age, with full, rounded breasts, all of the same age, and for them is a cup filled with wine. For them is all of this as a reward and a bounty from Allah, and a generous gift sufficient for them. (He is) the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful of this world and the Hereafter. They will not be able to speak to Him except concerning what He has permitted them. On the day when Jibril (peace be upon him) and the angels stand in rows, they will not intercede except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted to intercede, and he will speak what is true and correct. That is the true day, about whose occurrence there is no doubt. So whoever wills salvation from its terrors, let him take a path to his Lord as a place of return, through righteous deeds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 78, verse 40:

Indeed, We have warned you of the punishment of the Last Day, which is near, the Day on which every person will see what he did of good and what he earned of sin, and the disbeliever will say, from the terror of the reckoning: ﴿Oh, I wish I had been dust, and had not been resurrected.﴾
